links.outcome: Medical QA accuracy with versus without retrieved or curated external evidence across languages and model sizes
links.effect: External knowledge did not systematically improve performance. English web retrieval helped most for high-resource languages. English plus target-language retrieval helped low-resource languages. PubMed lacked multilingual coverage.
links.quote: These findings challenge the assumption that external knowledge systematically improves performance and reveal that effective strategies depend on both the source of language resources and on model scale.

unlisted_practices: Cross-lingual and multilingual retrieval strategies (English plus target-language evidence) to improve low-resource language medical QA
Using web-retrieved content versus curated repositories versus LLM-generated explanations as evidence sources

screen.reason: Empirically benchmarks different external evidence and multilingual retrieval grounding strategies for LLM-based medical question answering across high- and low-resource languages.
